name: Social Security contribution, s.33 insured (เงินสมทบกองทุนประกันสังคม)
authority: Social Security Act B.E.2533 (Council of State current consolidation, https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/alJWY29wVXFRUUo0WkF2MTEwSndpQT09): s.33 an employee aged not under 15 nor over 60 is insured — a status, so one hired under 15 is insured from 15, read on the period end (an insured person stays insured after 60 while employed; a hire over 60 does not enter); s.46 employer and insured each contribute at the ministerial rate on wages between the ministerial floor and ceiling, a fraction of 50 satang or more counting as one baht and less dropped, computed separately on each employer’s wages; s.47 deducted at every wage payment — assessed MONTH_TO_DATE: each payment deducts what the month’s wages paid so far owe less what the month has deducted, so the s.46 floor and ceiling stay the month’s (a weekly or semi-monthly payee is charged on its first payday once the month’s wage reaches the ceiling); s.5 wage (ค่าจ้าง) is money paid for work in normal working days and hours, including pay for holidays and leave days not worked — overtime and holiday-work pay are outside it, and a discretionary bonus, unused-leave pay and severance are not pay for normal working time and are left out (register TH-SS-13 notes the bonus exclusion as interpretation). Rate: Ministerial Regulation on contribution rates B.E.2565, cl.3(2) and Schedule B (https://infocenter.oic.go.th/FILEWEB/CABINFOCENTER2/DRAWER056/GENERAL/DATA0000/00000773.PDF), 5% each from 1 January 2023. Base: THB1,650 floor; ceiling THB15,000 to 31 December 2025. Flood relief: 3% each side for a registered employer in the nine southern provinces the 8 January 2026 notice lists, wage months December 2025–May 2026 (https://ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/documents/100888.pdf; entity fact `sso_flood_relief_area`). The notice’s THB283 s.39 amount is not an employer payroll charge. The base regulation B.E.2568 (Gazette vol.142 part 81 Kor, 12 December 2025) was read from the SSO’s copy (https://www.sso.go.th/wpr/download/download_by_pool_file/47755): cl.1 in force 1 January 2026, cl.2 repeals Ministerial Regulation No.7 (B.E.2538), cl.3 THB1,650–17,500 to 31 December 2028, THB1,650–20,000 1 January 2029 to 31 December 2031, THB1,650–23,000 from 1 January 2032. The flood-relief notice was read from the Gazette’s own PDF on 29 September 2026 (100888: Ministry of Labour notice under Social Security Act s.46/1 para.1, vol.143 special part 6 Ngor p.7, published 8 January 2026, signed 7 January 2026; cl.1 3% each side, cl.2 THB283 for s.39, cl.3 refund of an overpayment at an SSO office); an assessment made at 5% before 8 January 2026 is not corrected or refunded here (register TH-SS-02).

name: Personal income tax withheld on employment income, s.50(1) (ภาษีเงินได้หัก ณ ที่จ่าย)
authority: Revenue Code (https://www.rd.go.th/5937.html) s.50(1): the payer of s.40(1) income multiplies each payment by the number of payments due in the year, computes the tax under s.48, divides it by that number and withholds the quotient; a remainder of the division is added to the last withholding of the year. s.42 bis: 50% expense deduction, at most THB100,000 (Act No.44 B.E.2560). s.47(1)(ก): THB60,000 personal allowance; s.47(1)(ฌ): social-security contributions actually paid; s.47(3): a non-resident keeps the personal allowance (only the spouse and child allowances require the family to be in Thailand), and s.50(1)’s method does not turn on residence (the flat 15% applies to s.40(2) paid abroad), so residents and non-residents are withheld alike. s.48(1) table (Act No.44 s.12, https://www.rd.go.th/59670.html): 0–150,000 exempt; 5% to 300,000; 10% to 500,000; 15% to 750,000; 20% to 1,000,000; 25% to 2,000,000; 30% to 5,000,000; 35% above. Order P.96/2543 (https://www.rd.go.th/3558.html) cl.1(1): the number of payments is 12 for a monthly payee, or the actual remaining payments in the year of hire (hired 1 April → 9) — 24 for a semi-monthly and 52 for a weekly one (cl.1(1)(ข)–(ค)), each payment withheld (cl.1(3)) — here `year.payments`, the months, halves or weekly paydays from the join to the year end; cl.1(2) deductions as declared on ล.ย.01 from the start of the year (the social-security relief is read as this employment’s monthly employee contribution × the number of payments — at a semi-monthly or weekly cadence, by owner rule 2026-09-28 (register TH-PIT-02), the s.46 contribution on this payment taken to the month (`produced.SSO.employee_month_estimate`) × 12 over a full year, pro rata to the payments due, the ล.ย.01 declaration a payroll supplies; the other ล.ย.01 allowances are the employee’s declared annual total, election `ly01_deductions`, register TH-PIT-06); cl.1(3) the quotient each payment, the remainder on the year’s last payment; cl.1(4) a changed payment recomputes on the new amount; cl.1(5) an occasional payment (overtime, bonus, unused-leave pay) is withheld whole in its month as the annual tax on regular pay plus it, less the annual tax on regular pay alone. The quotient is truncated to the satang (the Act’s remainder is what the division leaves). Not modelled: the December true-up (cl.2) and final-month correction (cl.3), both a right of the payer ("มีสิทธิ"), not a duty; employer-borne tax (cl.1(7)–(8)); one-time exit payments, which cl.1 excludes (severance is withheld by scheme SEVERANCE_TAX) — except, by owner rule 2026-09-28 (register TH-PIT-05), the taxable remainder of an exit payment (lines SEVERANCE_PAY and NOTICE_IN_LIEU less the MR No.126 cl.2(51) exemption) where service is under five years: DG Notification No.45 cl.2(ก) gives it no s.48(5) route, the 2025 ภ.ง.ด.91 instructions list it with salary under s.40(1), taxed together with the year’s other income, and no Revenue order states its withholding, so s.50(1) para.1 is applied to it as a payment made once — added whole to the year’s regular pay by the cl.1(5) method this base already uses: the annual tax with it less the annual tax without it, withheld in the exit month; benefits in kind (TH-PIT-07). Tax year 2025 figures are unchanged (2025 ภ.ง.ด.91 instructions, https://www.rd.go.th/fileadmin/tax_pdf/pit/2568/Ins91_241268.pdf).

elections.label: Annual allowances declared on ล.ย.01
elections.description: Order P.96/2543 cl.1(2): the annualised tax deducts the allowances the employee declared on ล.ย.01 with copies of the evidence, from the start of the year whatever month they are paid — a donation only once actually paid. Enter the annual total of the declared allowances other than the THB60,000 personal allowance and this employment’s social-security contributions, which payroll already deducts (e.g. spouse THB60,000, s.47(1)(ข)). Unrecorded is none. Register TH-PIT-06: the class-by-class caps are not checked here.

name: Social Security contribution, s.33 insured (เงินสมทบกองทุนประกันสังคม)
authority: Social Security Act B.E.2533 (Council of State current consolidation, https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/alJWY29wVXFRUUo0WkF2MTEwSndpQT09): s.33 an employee aged not under 15 nor over 60 is insured — a status, so one hired under 15 is insured from 15, read on the period end (an insured person stays insured after 60 while employed; a hire over 60 does not enter); s.46 employer and insured each contribute at the ministerial rate on wages between the ministerial floor and ceiling, a fraction of 50 satang or more counting as one baht and less dropped, computed separately on each employer’s wages; s.47 deducted at every wage payment — assessed MONTH_TO_DATE: each payment deducts what the month’s wages paid so far owe less what the month has deducted, so the s.46 floor and ceiling stay the month’s (a weekly or semi-monthly payee is charged on its first payday once the month’s wage reaches the ceiling); s.5 wage (ค่าจ้าง) is money paid for work in normal working days and hours, including pay for holidays and leave days not worked — overtime and holiday-work pay are outside it, and a discretionary bonus, unused-leave pay and severance are not pay for normal working time and are left out (register TH-SS-13 notes the bonus exclusion as interpretation). name: Personal income tax withheld on employment income, s.50(1) (ภาษีเงินได้หัก ณ ที่จ่าย)
authority: Revenue Code (https://www.rd.go.th/5937.html) s.50(1): the payer of s.40(1) income multiplies each payment by the number of payments due in the year, computes the tax under s.48, divides it by that number and withholds the quotient; a remainder of the division is added to the last withholding of the year. s.42 bis: 50% expense deduction, at most THB100,000 (Act No.44 B.E.2560). s.47(1)(ก): THB60,000 personal allowance; s.47(1)(ฌ): social-security contributions actually paid; s.47(3): a non-resident keeps the personal allowance (only the spouse and child allowances require the family to be in Thailand), and s.50(1)’s method does not turn on residence (the flat 15% applies to s.40(2) paid abroad), so residents and non-residents are withheld alike. s.48(1) table (Act No.44 s.12, https://www.rd.go.th/59670.html): 0–150,000 exempt; 5% to 300,000; 10% to 500,000; 15% to 750,000; 20% to 1,000,000; 25% to 2,000,000; 30% to 5,000,000; 35% above. Order P.96/2543 (https://www.rd.go.th/3558.html) cl.1(1): the number of payments is 12 for a monthly payee, or the actual remaining payments in the year of hire (hired 1 April → 9) — 24 for a semi-monthly and 52 for a weekly one (cl.1(1)(ข)–(ค)), each payment withheld (cl.1(3)) — here `year.payments`, the months, halves or weekly paydays from the join to the year end; cl.1(2) deductions as declared on ล.ย.01 from the start of the year (the social-security relief is read as this employment’s monthly employee contribution × the number of payments — at a semi-monthly or weekly cadence, by owner rule 2026-09-28 (register TH-PIT-02), the s.46 contribution on this payment taken to the month (`produced.SSO.employee_month_estimate`) × 12 over a full year, pro rata to the payments due, the ล.ย.01 declaration a payroll supplies; the other ล.ย.01 allowances are the employee’s declared annual total, election `ly01_deductions`, register TH-PIT-06); cl.1(3) the quotient each payment, the remainder on the year’s last payment; cl.1(4) a changed payment recomputes on the new amount; cl.1(5) an occasional payment (overtime, bonus, unused-leave pay) is withheld whole in its month as the annual tax on regular pay plus it, less the annual tax on regular pay alone. The quotient is truncated to the satang (the Act’s remainder is what the division leaves). Not modelled: the December true-up (cl.2) and final-month correction (cl.3), both a right of the payer ("มีสิทธิ"), not a duty; employer-borne tax (cl.1(7)–(8)); one-time exit payments, which cl.1 excludes (severance is withheld by scheme SEVERANCE_TAX) — except, by owner rule 2026-09-28 (register TH-PIT-05), the taxable remainder of an exit payment (lines SEVERANCE_PAY and NOTICE_IN_LIEU less the MR No.126 cl.2(51) exemption) where service is under five years: DG Notification No.45 cl.2(ก) gives it no s.48(5) route, the 2025 ภ.ง.ด.91 instructions list it with salary under s.40(1), taxed together with the year’s other income, and no Revenue order states its withholding, so s.50(1) para.1 is applied to it as a payment made once — added whole to the year’s regular pay by the cl.1(5) method this base already uses: the annual tax with it less the annual tax without it, withheld in the exit month; benefits in kind (TH-PIT-07). Tax year 2025 figures are unchanged (2025 ภ.ง.ด.91 instructions, https://www.rd.go.th/fileadmin/tax_pdf/pit/2568/Ins91_241268.pdf).

elections.description: Order P.96/2543 cl.1(2): the annualised tax deducts the allowances the employee declared on ล.ย.01 with copies of the evidence, from the start of the year whatever month they are paid — a donation only once actually paid. name: Social Security contribution, s.33 insured (เงินสมทบกองทุนประกันสังคม)
authority: Social Security Act B.E.2533 (Council of State current consolidation, https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/alJWY29wVXFRUUo0WkF2MTEwSndpQT09): s.33 an employee aged not under 15 nor over 60 is insured — a status, so one hired under 15 is insured from 15, read on the period end (an insured person stays insured after 60 while employed; a hire over 60 does not enter); s.46 employer and insured each contribute at the ministerial rate on wages between the ministerial floor and ceiling, a fraction of 50 satang or more counting as one baht and less dropped, computed separately on each employer’s wages; s.47 deducted at every wage payment — assessed MONTH_TO_DATE: each payment deducts what the month’s wages paid so far owe less what the month has deducted, so the s.46 floor and ceiling stay the month’s (a weekly or semi-monthly payee is charged on its first payday once the month’s wage reaches the ceiling); s.5 wage (ค่าจ้าง) is money paid for work in normal working days and hours, including pay for holidays and leave days not worked — overtime and holiday-work pay are outside it, and a discretionary bonus, unused-leave pay and severance are not pay for normal working time and are left out (register TH-SS-13 notes the bonus exclusion as interpretation). Rate: Ministerial Regulation on contribution rates B.E.2565, cl.3(2) and Schedule B (https://infocenter.oic.go.th/FILEWEB/CABINFOCENTER2/DRAWER056/GENERAL/DATA0000/00000773.PDF), 5% each from 1 January 2023. Base: THB1,650 floor; ceiling THB17,500 from 1 January 2026 (ministerial regulation, https://ratchakitcha.soc.go.th/documents/98728.pdf). The base regulation B.E.2568 (Gazette vol.142 part 81 Kor, 12 December 2025) was read from the SSO’s copy (https://www.sso.go.th/wpr/download/download_by_pool_file/47755): cl.1 in force 1 January 2026, cl.2 repeals Ministerial Regulation No.7 (B.E.2538), cl.3 THB1,650–17,500 to 31 December 2028, THB1,650–20,000 1 January 2029 to 31 December 2031, THB1,650–23,000 from 1 January 2032. The flood-relief notice was read from the Gazette’s own PDF on 29 September 2026 (100888: Ministry of Labour notice under Social Security Act s.46/1 para.1, vol.143 special part 6 Ngor p.7, published 8 January 2026, signed 7 January 2026; cl.1 3% each side, cl.2 THB283 for s.39, cl.3 refund of an overpayment at an SSO office); an assessment made at 5% before 8 January 2026 is not corrected or refunded here (register TH-SS-02).

Enter the annual total of the declared allowances other than the THB60,000 personal allowance and this employment’s social-security contributions, which payroll already deducts (e.g. spouse THB60,000, s.47(1)(ข)). Unrecorded is none. Register TH-PIT-06: the class-by-class caps are not checked here.

name: Employee Welfare Fund contribution (กองทุนสงเคราะห์ลูกจ้าง)

elections.label: Member of the employer’s provident fund
elections.description: Labour Protection Act s.130: only a worker covered by a qualifying employer-provided provident fund is excluded. Record the fund registration and this worker’s membership references before excluding the worker.

elections.label: Voluntary Employee Welfare Fund member below ten workers

elections.description: The Department’s employer registration certificate and named-worker entry under LPA s.130.

name: Social Security contribution, s.33 insured (เงินสมทบกองทุนประกันสังคม)

name: Personal income tax withheld on employment income, s.50(1) (ภาษีเงินได้หัก ณ ที่จ่าย)
authority: Revenue Code (https://www.rd.go.th/5937.html) s.50(1): the payer of s.40(1) income multiplies each payment by the number of payments due in the year, computes the tax under s.48, divides it by that number and withholds the quotient; a remainder of the division is added to the last withholding of the year. s.42 bis: 50% expense deduction, at most THB100,000 (Act No.44 B.E.2560). s.47(1)(ก): THB60,000 personal allowance; s.47(1)(ฌ): social-security contributions actually paid; s.47(3): a non-resident keeps the personal allowance (only the spouse and child allowances require the family to be in Thailand), and s.50(1)’s method does not turn on residence (the flat 15% applies to s.40(2) paid abroad), so residents and non-residents are withheld alike. s.48(1) table (Act No.44 s.12, https://www.rd.go.th/59670.html): 0–150,000 exempt; 5% to 300,000; 10% to 500,000; 15% to 750,000; 20% to 1,000,000; 25% to 2,000,000; 30% to 5,000,000; 35% above. Order P.96/2543 (https://www.rd.go.th/3558.html) cl.1(1): the number of payments is 12 for a monthly payee, or the actual remaining payments in the year of hire (hired 1 April → 9) — 24 for a semi-monthly and 52 for a weekly one (cl.1(1)(ข)–(ค)), each payment withheld (cl.1(3)) — here `year.payments`, the months, halves or weekly paydays from the join to the year end; cl.1(2) deductions as declared on ล.ย.01 from the start of the year (the social-security relief is read as this employment’s monthly employee contribution × the number of payments — at a semi-monthly or weekly cadence, by owner rule 2026-09-28 (register TH-PIT-02), the s.46 contribution on this payment taken to the month (`produced.SSO.employee_month_estimate`) × 12 over a full year, pro rata to the payments due, the ล.ย.01 declaration a payroll supplies; the other ล.ย.01 allowances are the employee’s declared annual total, election `ly01_deductions`, register TH-PIT-06); cl.1(3) the quotient each payment, the remainder on the year’s last payment; cl.1(4) a changed payment recomputes on the new amount; cl.1(5) an occasional payment (overtime, bonus, unused-leave pay) is withheld whole in its month as the annual tax on regular pay plus it, less the annual tax on regular pay alone. The quotient is truncated to the satang (the Act’s remainder is what the division leaves). Not modelled: the December true-up (cl.2) and final-month correction (cl.3), both a right of the payer ("มีสิทธิ"), not a duty; employer-borne tax (cl.1(7)–(8)); one-time exit payments, which cl.1 excludes (severance is withheld by scheme SEVERANCE_TAX) — except, by owner rule 2026-09-28 (register TH-PIT-05), the taxable remainder of an exit payment (lines SEVERANCE_PAY and NOTICE_IN_LIEU less the MR No.126 cl.2(51) exemption) where service is under five years: DG Notification No.45 cl.2(ก) gives it no s.48(5) route, the 2025 ภ.ง.ด.91 instructions list it with salary under s.40(1), taxed together with the year’s other income, and no Revenue order states its withholding, so s.50(1) para.1 is applied to it as a payment made once — added whole to the year’s regular pay by the cl.1(5) method this base already uses: the annual tax with it less the annual tax without it, withheld in the exit month; benefits in kind (TH-PIT-07). Tax year 2025 figures are unchanged (2025 ภ.ง.ด.91 instructions, https://www.rd.go.th/fileadmin/tax_pdf/pit/2568/Ins91_241268.pdf).

Order P.96/2543 (https://www.rd.go.th/3558.html) cl.1(1): the number of payments is 12 for a monthly payee, or the actual remaining payments in the year of hire (hired 1 April → 9) — 24 for a semi-monthly and 52 for a weekly one (cl.1(1)(ข)–(ค)), each payment withheld (cl.1(3)) — here `year.payments`, the months, halves or weekly paydays from the join to the year end; cl.1(2) deductions as declared on ล.ย.01 from the start of the year (the social-security relief is read as this employment’s monthly employee contribution × the number of payments — at a semi-monthly or weekly cadence, by owner rule 2026-09-28 (register TH-PIT-02), the s.46 contribution on this payment taken to the month (`produced.SSO.employee_month_estimate`) × 12 over a full year, pro rata to the payments due, the ล.ย.01 declaration a payroll supplies; the other ล.ย.01 allowances are the employee’s declared annual total, election `ly01_deductions`, register TH-PIT-06); cl.1(3) the quotient each payment, the remainder on the year’s last payment; cl.1(4) a changed payment recomputes on the new amount; cl.1(5) an occasional payment (overtime, bonus, unused-leave pay) is withheld whole in its month as the annual tax on regular pay plus it, less the annual tax on regular pay alone. The quotient is truncated to the satang (the Act’s remainder is what the division leaves). Not modelled: the December true-up (cl.2) and final-month correction (cl.3), both a right of the payer ("มีสิทธิ"), not a duty; employer-borne tax (cl.1(7)–(8)); one-time exit payments, which cl.1 excludes (severance is withheld by scheme SEVERANCE_TAX) — except, by owner rule 2026-09-28 (register TH-PIT-05), the taxable remainder of an exit payment (lines SEVERANCE_PAY and NOTICE_IN_LIEU less the MR No.126 cl.2(51) exemption) where service is under five years: DG Notification No.45 cl.2(ก) gives it no s.48(5) route, the 2025 ภ.ง.ด.91 instructions list it with salary under s.40(1), taxed together with the year’s other income, and no Revenue order states its withholding, so s.50(1) para.1 is applied to it as a payment made once — added whole to the year’s regular pay by the cl.1(5) method this base already uses: the annual tax with it less the annual tax without it, withheld in the exit month; benefits in kind (TH-PIT-07). Tax year 2025 figures are unchanged (2025 ภ.ง.ด.91 instructions, https://www.rd.go.th/fileadmin/tax_pdf/pit/2568/Ins91_241268.pdf).

name: Employee Welfare Fund contribution (กองทุนสงเคราะห์ลูกจ้าง)
authority: Labour Protection Act ss.130–131 (https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/ZGN3NXk0eENvNjBSdjRnT2NsdjFTQT09): s.130 establishes coverage for businesses with at least ten employees, exempts qualifying employer-provided provident funds or other exit/death welfare, and permits voluntary membership under Committee rules with worker request, employer consent and Department registration certificate; s.131 requires the employee and employer contributions at each wage payment from fund membership. name: Tax withheld on severance, s.50(1) para.3 and s.48(5) (ภาษีหัก ณ ที่จ่าย เงินได้เพราะเหตุออกจากงาน)
authority: Revenue Code (https://www.rd.go.th/5937.html) s.50(1) para.3: a one-time payment on leaving, computed from years of service and paid under the Director-General’s criteria, is withheld as the tax computed under s.48(5): the payment less 7,000 × years of service (a part year of 183 days or more counting as a year, less dropped), less a further 50% of the rest, taxed on the s.48(1) table. Director-General Notification on income tax No.45 (https://www.rd.go.th/3213.html) cl.1(ค): statutory severance is such a payment; cl.2(ก) (as amended by No.252): service of at least five years; cl.4: the s.50(1) withholding follows cls.2–3. Ministerial Regulation No.126 cl.2(51) (as amended by No.394 B.E.2567, for income from 1 January 2023; https://www.rd.go.th/2502.html): severance under the Labour Protection Act is exempt up to the wage of the last 400 days and at most THB600,000, except severance on retirement or contract expiry (the 2025 ภ.ง.ด.91 instructions state the same). cl.1(ง): any other one-time payment on leaving, such as s.17/1 pay in lieu of notice (line NOTICE_IN_LIEU), is such a payment too and joins the base, outside the exemption. Order P.96/2543 cl.1 excludes one-time exit payments from the regular method, so this line never enters PIT. Readings: the exemption is applied to the SEVERANCE_PAY line alone (MR No.126 cl.2(51) exempts severance under the Act, not notice pay); the last-400-day wage is 400 × the s.118 day (monthly ÷ 30); special severance (ss.120–122) carried on the SEVERANCE_PAY line is treated as severance under the Act for the exemption. Under five years’ service (no s.48(5) route, DG No.45 cl.2(ก)) this line withholds nothing: the taxable remainder above the exemption is withheld on the PIT line instead (owner rule 2026-09-28, register TH-PIT-05). Not modelled: service carried across employers through a provident-fund transfer (No.252). Register TH-PIT-05.

name: Social Security contribution, s.33 insured (เงินสมทบกองทุนประกันสังคม)
authority: Social Security Act B.E.2533 (Council of State current consolidation, https://searchlaw.ocs.go.th/council-of-state/#/public/doc/alJWY29wVXFRUUo0WkF2MTEwSndpQT09): s.33 an employee aged not under 15 nor over 60 is insured — a status, so one hired under 15 is insured from 15, read on the period end (an insured person stays insured after 60 while employed; a hire over 60 does not enter); s.46 employer and insured each contribute at the ministerial rate on wages between the ministerial floor and ceiling, a fraction of 50 satang or more counting as one baht and less dropped, computed separately on each employer’s wages; s.47 deducted at every wage payment — assessed MONTH_TO_DATE: each payment deducts what the month’s wages paid so far owe less what the month has deducted, so the s.46 floor and ceiling stay the month’s (a weekly or semi-monthly payee is charged on its first payday once the month’s wage reaches the ceiling); s.5 wage (ค่าจ้าง) is money paid for work in normal working days and hours, including pay for holidays and leave days not worked — overtime and holiday-work pay are outside it, and a discretionary bonus, unused-leave pay and severance are not pay for normal working time and are left out (register TH-SS-13 notes the bonus exclusion as interpretation). name: Personal income tax withheld on employment income, s.50(1) (ภาษีเงินได้หัก ณ ที่จ่าย)
authority: Revenue Code (https://www.rd.go.th/5937.html) s.50(1): the payer of s.40(1) income multiplies each payment by the number of payments due in the year, computes the tax under s.48, divides it by that number and withholds the quotient; a remainder of the division is added to the last withholding of the year. s.42 bis: 50% expense deduction, at most THB100,000 (Act No.44 B.E.2560). s.47(1)(ก): THB60,000 personal allowance; s.47(1)(ฌ): social-security contributions actually paid; s.47(3): a non-resident keeps the personal allowance (only the spouse and child allowances require the family to be in Thailand), and s.50(1)’s method does not turn on residence (the flat 15% applies to s.40(2) paid abroad), so residents and non-residents are withheld alike. s.48(1) table (Act No.44 s.12, https://www.rd.go.th/59670.html): 0–150,000 exempt; 5% to 300,000; 10% to 500,000; 15% to 750,000; 20% to 1,000,000; 25% to 2,000,000; 30% to 5,000,000; 35% above. Order P.96/2543 (https://www.rd.go.th/3558.html) cl.1(1): the number of payments is 12 for a monthly payee, or the actual remaining payments in the year of hire (hired 1 April → 9) — 24 for a semi-monthly and 52 for a weekly one (cl.1(1)(ข)–(ค)), each payment withheld (cl.1(3)) — here `year.payments`, the months, halves or weekly paydays from the join to the year end; cl.1(2) deductions as declared on ล.ย.01 from the start of the year (the social-security relief is read as this employment’s monthly employee contribution × the number of payments — at a semi-monthly or weekly cadence, by owner rule 2026-09-28 (register TH-PIT-02), the s.46 contribution on this payment taken to the month (`produced.SSO.employee_month_estimate`) × 12 over a full year, pro rata to the payments due, the ล.ย.01 declaration a payroll supplies; the other ล.ย.01 allowances are the employee’s declared annual total, election `ly01_deductions`, register TH-PIT-06); cl.1(3) the quotient each payment, the remainder on the year’s last payment; cl.1(4) a changed payment recomputes on the new amount; cl.1(5) an occasional payment (overtime, bonus, unused-leave pay) is withheld whole in its month as the annual tax on regular pay plus it, less the annual tax on regular pay alone. The quotient is truncated to the satang (the Act’s remainder is what the division leaves). name: Tax withheld on severance, s.50(1) para.3 and s.48(5) (ภาษีหัก ณ ที่จ่าย เงินได้เพราะเหตุออกจากงาน)
authority: Revenue Code (https://www.rd.go.th/5937.html) s.50(1) para.3: a one-time payment on leaving, computed from years of service and paid under the Director-General’s criteria, is withheld as the tax computed under s.48(5): the payment less 7,000 × years of service (a part year of 183 days or more counting as a year, less dropped), less a further 50% of the rest, taxed on the s.48(1) table. Director-General Notification on income tax No.45 (https://www.rd.go.th/3213.html) cl.1(ค): statutory severance is such a payment; cl.2(ก) (as amended by No.252): service of at least five years; cl.4: the s.50(1) withholding follows cls.2–3. Ministerial Regulation No.126 cl.2(51) (as amended by No.394 B.E.2567, for income from 1 January 2023; https://www.rd.go.th/2502.html): severance under the Labour Protection Act is exempt up to the wage of the last 400 days and at most THB600,000, except severance on retirement or contract expiry (the 2025 ภ.ง.ด.91 instructions state the same). cl.1(ง): any other one-time payment on leaving, such as s.17/1 pay in lieu of notice (line NOTICE_IN_LIEU), is such a payment too and joins the base, outside the exemption. Order P.96/2543 cl.1 excludes one-time exit payments from the regular method, so this line never enters PIT. Readings: the exemption is applied to the SEVERANCE_PAY line alone (MR No.126 cl.2(51) exempts severance under the Act, not notice pay); the last-400-day wage is 400 × the s.118 day (monthly ÷ 30); special severance (ss.120–122) carried on the SEVERANCE_PAY line is treated as severance under the Act for the exemption. Under five years’ service (no s.48(5) route, DG No.45 cl.2(ก)) this line withholds nothing: the taxable remainder above the exemption is withheld on the PIT line instead (owner rule 2026-09-28, register TH-PIT-05). Not modelled: service carried across employers through a provident-fund transfer (No.252). Register TH-PIT-05.
